newsitem.title: USA: Vanadium prices look to firm further - Stratcor.
newsitem.headline: Vanadium prices look to firm further - Stratcor.

text.p: Vanadium prices look set to rise further because of continuing short-term tightness in supply pipelines, William Beattie, president of Strategic Minerals Corp said.
"Prices will continue to firm," Beattie told reporters. "That's what one might conclude from some of the talk in the market place."
The market was suffering from short-term dislocation due to low inventories which caused prices to climb in recent weeks.
Beattie said pentoxide prices could well rise to $4.00 per pound, with ferro-vanadium in "the neighbourhood" of $20 per kilo.
Ferro-vanadium is currently about $17 to $18 per kilo, with pentoxide at about $3.50 per pound.
"But we think there is more than adequate supply to take care of long term needs of vanadium," Beattie said.
"The vanadium market will grow 3 to 4 percent a year, and it will be in excess of the rate of (general) steel production because HSLA steel growth is stronger," he added.
HSLA steels are used in machinery, construction and auto parts.
Beattie pegged global vanadium production at 130 million pounds a year, led by Highveld Steel and Vanadium Corp of South Africa, with Glencore International in third place, just following Stratcor.
Stratcor employs 550 people worldwide and has a turnover of some $100 million from vanadium, its main business.
